author: EMILY HYATT/The History Center
title: Diboll Day offered patriotic themes leading up to bicentennial | Community | lufkindailynews.com
text:
It is finally time to celebrate the United States’ 250th birthday, and local organizations are offering fireworks, festivities, food and fun for Angelina County to enjoy. Regardless of political opinions, religious views or any of the other things that divide us, on this July Fourth, locals can gather to commemorate and celebrate. The History Center is proud to offer our Happy Birthday, U.S.A. exhibit as part of the commemoration events. We hope looking back at the two-year celebration in 1976 has provided inspiration for partygoers this year. The History Center is closed July 3-5 but will reopen on July 6 with regular hours, and the exhibit will be up through the fall.
While most of this year’s celebration will happen on July Fourth, the bicentennial stretched for all of 1975 and 1976. The longer period of commemoration allowed other events to take the patriotic theme, including Diboll Day 1976. Eventual Queen Lisa Burkhalter and her fellow candidates dressed in patriotic clothes, parade floats featured patriotic themes and as much red, white and blue as the town could find, and supporting events kept with the Spirit of 1976. Diboll pulled out all the stops to raise money and to honor the United States and its birthday.
